claims.text: The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has a relatively coarse grain structure.
The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has minimal Cu segregation.
The baseline coating does not form a uniform continuous oxide film during high-temperature sliding.
Post-deposition annealing will refine the FeNiCrCoCu coating to a nanocrystalline grain structure.
Post-deposition annealing will drive Cu diffusion and segregation to grain boundaries.
During high-temperature sliding, grain-boundary-segregated Cu will oxidize rapidly.
Oxidation of segregated Cu will form a continuous Cu-rich tribofilm, such as CuO.
The Cu-rich oxide tribofilm will be lubricious.
The continuous Cu-rich oxide film will distribute applied stresses more uniformly along refined grain boundaries.
The annealing-induced structure and oxide film will shift deformation from bulk dislocation motion toward grain-boundary-mediated plasticity.
The proposed mechanism will reduce localized shear during sliding.
The annealed coating will have a lower wear rate than the as-deposited baseline.
The annealed coating will have a lower coefficient of friction than the as-deposited baseline.
The annealed coating will exhibit more intergranular, grain-boundary-controlled plasticity and less dislocation-dominated slip.
The predicted behavior is expected during sliding in air at 300–600 °C on conventional metal substrates.
Changes in oxygen availability, sliding speed, or contact load may alter oxide formation and deformation mechanisms.
The required Cu-segregation level and oxide-film thickness for optimal wear resistance are not known.
